steps.title: The orbit
steps.say: The Earth travels once a year around the Sun. Seasons are not caused by the Earth being closer to or farther from the Sun.

steps.title: The tilted axis
steps.say: The Earth's axis is tilted 23.5 degrees, and it always points the same way in space. So during the year, the northern hemisphere leans toward the Sun for half the orbit and away for the other half.

steps.title: Winter in the north
steps.say: Half a year later the northern hemisphere leans away from the Sun. The Sun's rays hit it at a slant, so they are spread out and weaker, and the days are shorter.

steps.title: Equinoxes
steps.say: At the equinoxes neither hemisphere leans toward the Sun, and the Sun is directly overhead at the equator. Spring and autumn are the transitions between the two extremes.

steps.title: Quiz
steps.say: Now you try it. Drag the Earth to the point where it is summer in the southern hemisphere.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.say: Drag the Earth around its orbit and watch how the sunlight on the surface changes with the season.
